narratives.Overview:
1. Added lines, git mode. When the change set is git-enumerated, the check runs one `git diff -U0 --no-renames --no-color --no-ext-diff --no-textconv <mergeBase> -- <paths>` (working tree against the same merge base that produced the change set) over the paths that reach the class 2 scan, and reads the added line numbers with `parseUnifiedDiffAddedLines` (`packages/core/src/forward-coverage/diff-lines.ts`). That parser is fixed in the same PR: it reads the old and new line counts from each `@@` header (a missing count is 1; a no-newline marker line (it starts with a backslash) does not count) and treats every line until both counts are used up as hunk payload, so payload that starts with `+++ `, `--- ` or `diff --git ` never changes the current file or ends the hunk. Headers are recognised only outside a hunk. `verify:forward-coverage`, the parser's other user, gets the same fix.
2. Added lines, injected mode. When `changedFiles` is injected, the only source is a new optional `ClassCheckOptions.addedLines` (path to the set of 1-based added line numbers). Injected mode never reads base text or diffs from git.
3. Fail closed. A path with no added-line entry is scanned on every line, as today. This covers untracked files, files git treats as binary, a failed diff, and injected paths without an entry. A file absent at the merge base, and a rename target (renames are off), get an entry that lists every line, so they are fully scanned too.
4. Scan. Head content is split on `\n` with one trailing `\r` stripped per line. The existing roots, skips and needle regexes run on the added lines only. No whitespace normalisation and no line matching: a moved or re-indented reference line is an added line and fails. Still one finding per file; `detail` names the first added line that matches.
5. Presentation coverage. `presentation-coverage/gates.ts` passes `addedLines` from `git diff -U0 --no-renames --no-color --no-ext-diff --no-textconv <mergeBase> <candidate> -- <changed paths>`, parsed the same way. A failed diff passes no entries (fail closed).
6. No change to `verify:test-boundary`; it stays the full-repo audit and keeps reporting old references.
7. One PR. Files: `packages/core/src/class-checks/evaluate.ts`, `evaluate.test.ts`, `packages/core/src/forward-coverage/diff-lines.ts` and its test, `packages/core/src/presentation-coverage/gates.ts` and its test, the evaluator-surface disclosure `xbrief/evaluator-surface-disposition.json`, one `changelog.d/` fragment. No new verb, flag, policy field or numeric constant.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a production file whose merge-base copy already holds a test-root reference, when the diff changes only another line of that file, then class 2 reports no finding for that file.
- Given that file, when the diff adds a new line with a test-root reference, then class 2 fails and names the file.
- Given that file, when the diff deletes the reference line and adds the same text elsewhere in the file, then class 2 fails.
- Given that file, when the diff only re-indents the reference line, then class 2 fails.
- Given an untracked or new production file with a test-root reference, then class 2 fails as today.
- Given injected `changedFiles` and `fileContents` with no `addedLines` entry for a path, then every line of that path is scanned (the existing injected class 2 tests pass unchanged).
- Given injected `addedLines` for a path, then class 2 fails only when a reference is on a listed line.
- Given a diff whose added lines include a line starting with `++ ` followed by an added line with a test-root reference, then class 2 fails; and `parseUnifiedDiffAddedLines` returns both added line numbers for that file and no entry for a bogus path.
- Given a presentation-coverage composed run, an unrelated edit to a file whose base already holds a reference gives `verify:class-checks` code 0, and an added reference line gives code 1.
- Given a pre-existing reference, `verify:test-boundary` still reports it.
narratives.Constraint:
- A line multiset or any whole-file set comparison against the base (comment 7084606488 finding 1).
- Trimming or normalising whitespace before comparison (finding 1; Stop 1 question 2).
- Reading base text or a diff from ambient git for injected inputs (finding 2).
- Leaving the presentation-coverage caller on the whole-file scan (finding 2; question 5).
- Using `parseUnifiedDiffAddedLines` without the hunk-length fix (audit 7084658145 finding 1).
- A policy allow entry for `drift-gate.ts`, or moving its reference, in place of this fix.

## In plain English
`verify:class-checks` is a fail-closed fence over the files a diff touches. Its class 2 fails when a production file (under a source root, or deploy-shaped) names a test or fixture root such as `tests/`. Today it scans the whole content of each touched file and never looks at the base revision. So a file that already named a test root before class checks existed cannot be edited at all: any edit, even one line elsewhere in the file, fails class 2. `packages/core/src/xbrief-migrate/drift-gate.ts` is the live case: its built-in allow list holds `"tests/**"` (last changed by #4163, before class checks shipped in #5005), and the #4905 fix edits a different function in that file. Class checks have no approve or skip, so the only exits today are moving the reference or a policy allow entry in a separate PR.

The recommended fix: class 2 reports a reference only when the diff adds it. For each touched production file, the check reads the same path at the merge base and counts a matched line only when that line is not already in the base file (a line multiset, so a copied or second reference still counts as new). A missing base file (new file, rename, unreadable blob) counts every reference as new, as today. The full-repo audit (`verify:test-boundary`, which reads every tracked file) keeps reporting old references.

## Operator direction (Scott, 2026-11-22; relayed by the coordinator; recorded as constraints)
- "fix 7077 first", chosen instead of a policy allow entry for `drift-gate.ts`.
- Coordinator constraint for this arc: the fix must not let a diff add a new test-root reference to production code.

## Pains
- P1 — A production file that already named a test or fixture root at the base cannot be edited at all: any change fails class 2 even when the diff adds no reference, and class checks offer no approve or skip (#7077; blocks #4905 and, behind it, #7025).

## Out of scope (named, not pains)
- Class 3 (`test-identity-in-infra`, `scanTestIdentityInInfra`) also scans whole content; it is not changed here.
- Which paths count as production, which roots are forbidden, and the needle regexes in `scanProductionReferences`.
- `verify:test-boundary`'s own reference scan (`packages/core/src/test-boundary/evaluate.ts`), which stays the full-repo audit.
- Class 1, class 4, and the same-PR policy-edit check.
- Removing the `"tests/**"` reference from `drift-gate.ts` or adding a policy allow entry for it.

## Evidence
- #7077 body: `drift-gate.ts` keeps `"tests/**"` in its built-in allow list and the #4905 product commit (it edits `scanCorpusToken` only) cannot pass class 2.

## Anchors at the dispatch SHA
- `packages/core/src/class-checks/evaluate.ts` 58-70 `ClassCheckOptions` (`baseRef`, `changedFiles`, `fileContents`, injected policies). 153-162 `candidateTreeBase` (merge base of base ref and HEAD; falls back to the base ref). 164-249 `changedFilesVsBase` (working tree against the merge base plus untracked files; returns `mergeBase`). 318-323 `readAtRef` (`git show <ref>:<path>`, null on any failure). 624-682 `scanProductionReferences` (skips test files, test/fixture roots and CI harness workflows; production = under a source root or deploy-shaped; builds two regexes per forbidden root and tests them against the whole content; returns one finding per file). 768-785 `readContent` (injected map or working-tree read, capped at 512000 chars). 815 and 856 `candidateMergeBase` (null when `changedFiles` is injected). 951-956 the class 2 call (skips protected globs and base allow-listed paths). 1021-1043 same-PR policy edit that would clear a class 1/2 hit.
- `packages/core/src/class-checks/evaluate.test.ts` 130-144 (class 2 with injected `changedFiles`/`fileContents` and project root `/tmp/proj`); 492-507, 533-604, 631-701, 721-740 (more injected class 2 cases); 758-849 (git fixture: `master` base, `story` branch, working tree against the merge base).
- `packages/core/src/presentation-coverage/gates.ts` 157-183: calls `evaluateClassChecks` with `baseRef: mergeBase`, injected `changedFiles`, head `fileContents` and base policies; a `base.read` reader is in scope (102-121).
- `packages/core/src/pre-pr-controller/controller.ts` 138: calls `evaluateClassChecks(root, { baseRef })` (git-enumerated path).
- `packages/core/src/test-boundary/evaluate.ts` 1-7, 52-70 (`git ls-files`), 393-420 (reference scan over every tracked file): the full-repo audit.
- `packages/core/src/xbrief-migrate/drift-gate.ts` 66 (`"tests/**"`).

## Recommended mechanism (the thing to critique)
- D1. Base text. For each changed path that reaches the class 2 call, read the base text once: `readAtRef(root, candidateMergeBase ?? baseRef, path)`, capped like `readContent`. Null (new file, rename target, deleted at base, git failure, no git) means no base text.
- D2. New lines only. Split head and base text into lines; strip a trailing `\r` and outer whitespace from each line for the comparison. Build a multiset of base lines. Walk head lines in order; a head line whose text is still in the base multiset consumes one copy and is skipped; every other head line is a candidate line.
- D3. Scan. Run the existing per-root needle regexes on candidate lines only (same production test, same roots, same skips). Report one finding per file as today, naming the first new matching line number in `detail`. With no base text every head line is a candidate, so behavior equals today's.
- D4. Seam. Add optional `baseFileContents?: ReadonlyMap<string, string | null>` beside `fileContents`. When present it is the base source (absent key or null = no base text) and no git read happens. `presentation-coverage/gates.ts` passes it from `base.read` for the changed paths. When `fileContents` is injected without `baseFileContents`, the base read falls back to git at `baseRef` (so a non-git project root keeps today's behavior).
- D5. Audit. No change to `verify:test-boundary`; it keeps reporting old references repo-wide.
- D6. Tests: pre-existing reference plus an unrelated edit in the same file (pass); a new reference line added to a file that already has one (fail); a copied existing reference line (fail); a re-indented existing line (pass); CRLF working tree against an LF blob (pass); new file (fail as today); injected `baseFileContents` cases; existing tests unchanged.
- D7. Scope. One PR: `class-checks/evaluate.ts`, `evaluate.test.ts`, `presentation-coverage/gates.ts`, the evaluator-surface disclosure (`xbrief/evaluator-surface-disposition.json`), one `changelog.d/` fragment.

Questions for the critic:
1. Line multiset (D2) or a diff hunk parse of added lines? Which one leaves no way to add a new reference unreported, and which is cheaper to keep right on Windows line endings and on injected inputs?
2. Is trimming outer whitespace safe, or does it open a hole (for example a reference line moved into a different construct)?
3. Should the base be the merge base, or `baseRef` when the merge base is unknown? Is a git read failure correctly treated as "no base text" (fail closed)?
4. Is D4's fallback (injected head contents, git base read) right, or should injected mode stay hermetic?
5. Does the presentation-coverage caller need to change in this PR, or can it keep today's whole-file scan?
6. Does this fit one PR for the next build?

## In plain English

The current check blocks unrelated edits because it treats every old reference as newly introduced. Comparing against the base can fix that, but the proposed line multiset also forgives moving an existing reference into a different construct. It therefore cannot support the stated promise that added references remain reported. The design needs a precise definition of “new” before it binds.

## Answers to Stop 1

1. **Prefer added-line comparison for the stated constraint.** A line multiset detects increased counts but loses location and order. An ordered comparison preserves more information. Neither approach guarantees detection of semantic changes made entirely through surrounding lines; the contract should describe lexical added-line detection.
2. **Normalize CRLF, but do not generally trim outer whitespace.** Indentation can change meaning in YAML and Python. Movement is a separate problem that exists even without trimming.
3. **Use the same resolved base that produced the changed-file set.** Treating missing or unreadable base text as no exemption is conservative. Using `baseRef` is appropriate when it explicitly identifies the caller’s comparison snapshot; an unknown merge base is not evidence that an arbitrary branch tip is equivalent.
4. **Keep injected content hermetic for this comparison.** If injected head text lacks injected base text, scan all head lines. Ambient Git should not silently grant exemptions.
5. **Change the presentation-coverage caller in this PR.** It already owns both snapshots and should supply the base map. Otherwise the two entry points retain different behavior.
6. **Yes, one PR**, including caller-level regression coverage. The work is small enough, but the comparison contract needs correction first.

## Findings

### 1. blocks-the-design — A line multiset forgives relocation, not just old references

**Evidence:** Stop 1 D2 consumes matching lines anywhere in the base file. I ran an in-memory Node reproduction of that algorithm:

```text
Base:                       Head:
const docs = [              const docs = [
  "tests/fixtures",          ];
];                          const shipped = [
const shipped = [             "tests/fixtures",
];                          ];
```

The candidate-line result was `[]`. A second check copying the reference without deleting the original correctly returned the extra line.

At the pin, `packages/core/src/class-checks/evaluate.ts:624–677` performs lexical matching without interpreting the surrounding construct. Production classification includes deployment files and pipelines at lines 644–649.

**Failure mode:** Deleting an old occurrence provides credit for adding the same text elsewhere. Trimming extends that exemption to indentation changes, including potentially meaningful YAML nesting changes. D6’s copied-line test does not exercise deletion plus relocation.

**Disposition consequence:** D2 cannot bind under the current no-new-reference claim. Prefer ordered added-line comparison with CRLF normalization and explicit movement/indentation tests. State the guarantee as detecting matching added lines, not detecting every newly effective dependency.

The strongest case for the multiset is simplicity: it is portable, handles injected strings, and tolerates formatting and reordering. I would accept it if the constraint explicitly allowed relocation and defined “new” as increased normalized-line multiplicity. That is weaker than the current stated constraint.

Existing mechanism: `packages/core/src/forward-coverage/diff-lines.ts:105–161` already exports `parseUnifiedDiffAddedLines` and handles CRLF diff records. It is a parser, not a complete solution for generating diffs between injected strings; that remaining seam must be addressed.

### 2. sharpens-framing — Injected snapshots should own their exemptions

**Evidence:** At the pin, `packages/core/src/class-checks/evaluate.ts:773–775` treats an injected head map as authoritative. Lines 813–817 leave `candidateMergeBase` null for injected changed files. D4 would then obtain exemption text from ambient Git unless a base map is supplied.

`packages/core/src/presentation-coverage/gates.ts:97–118` already holds `base`, `head`, and `mergeBase`; lines 171–180 inject head contents and policies into class checks.

**Failure mode:** Identical injected head inputs can produce different findings depending on the repository behind `projectRoot`. A caller that omitted the new optional map can accidentally receive exemptions from a different snapshot. This is particularly relevant when snapshots and a shared checkout are evaluated at different times.

**Disposition consequence:** The base-map seam is sound, but its default should be conservative: injected head without injected base means no base exemption. The presentation caller should supply its existing base reader’s results. Add a caller-level test showing both an unrelated edit passing and an added reference failing.

### 3. footnote — The envelope ceiling differs from the single-seat rule

**Evidence:** The envelope names ceiling `7084569438`, matching the supplied panel deposit. The pinned contract’s `### Envelope and ceiling` instead specifies the triage write-back as the round-one ceiling when one exists for a single critic. Here that write-back is `7084567590`; spend is N=1.

**Failure mode:** The dispatch record applies the panel-deposit ceiling convention to a single-seat round.

**Disposition consequence:** No product-design consequence. I honored the explicit envelope ceiling and read nothing after it; the deposit contained dispatch metadata rather than sibling findings.

## Verification and limits

I read the supplied snapshot and used SHA-pinned `git show` reads plus `git grep` to inspect the evaluator, snapshot caller, full-repo audit, and existing diff parser. I ran the two in-memory multiset checks above. I did not run repository tests, install dependencies, modify files, or post comments.

The indentation and surrounding-context arguments are my technical reasoning, not executed language-parser tests. The existing working-tree reader truncates at 512,000 characters (`class-checks/evaluate.ts:779–780`), so any detection guarantee also remains bounded by the existing scan limit. USER.md access was denied; no addressing preference was inferred.

**Lean:** first successor lean under Stop 1 7084567590 (round 1: 1 of 1 critic posted, comment 7084606488)

## In plain English
Problem: class 2 of `verify:class-checks` scans the whole content of every production file a diff touches and never looks at the base. A file that already named a test root (for example `"tests/**"` in `drift-gate.ts`) cannot be edited at all, and class checks have no approve or skip (#7077).

What the critic found: comparing against the base is right, but the Stop 1 line multiset is not. It forgives a reference that is deleted in one place and added in another, and trimming whitespace forgives a re-indent that can change meaning in YAML or Python. The critic also found that injected inputs must not borrow base text from the git repository behind the project root, and that the presentation-coverage caller must supply its own base so both entry points behave the same.

Solution this lean proposes: class 2 scans only the lines that git's diff against the merge base marks as added. The check gets those line numbers from one `git diff -U0` run, read with the parser Directive already has (`parseUnifiedDiffAddedLines`). Injected callers pass the added lines themselves; a path with no added-line data is scanned on every line, as today. No whitespace or line-matching rules of our own.

What this adds: one git diff call, one optional input, and a line filter in front of the existing needle regexes.

What it removes: the whole-file scan for files git can diff against the merge base.

What it does not do:
- It does not judge the effect of unchanged lines; the guarantee is lexical: a test-root reference on an added line fails.
- It does not change which files count as production, the forbidden roots, the needle regexes, class 1, 3 or 4, or the same-PR policy-edit check.
- It does not change `verify:test-boundary`, which keeps reporting old references across the whole repo.
If confirmed, the synthesis would assert this design. Leftover next-build: none.

### 1. blocks-the-design — Added source text can redirect the diff parser

**Evidence:** At the dispatch pin, `packages/core/src/forward-coverage/diff-lines.ts:122–134` recognizes `+++ ` as a file header before checking whether it is inside a hunk. It changes the current path and clears `inHunk`. Lines 142–143 then discard subsequent additions until another hunk header.

I loaded the exact pinned TypeScript through `git show`, stripped types using Node’s `stripTypeScriptTypes`, and executed the exported parser in memory with this patch:

```diff
diff --git a/src/a.ts b/src/a.ts
--- a/src/a.ts
+++ b/src/a.ts
@@ -1 +1,3 @@
-old
+new
+++ counter;
+const p = "tests/new";
```

The result was:

```text
src/a.ts -> {1}
counter; -> {}
```

The added source line `++ counter;` becomes `+++ counter;` in unified diff syntax. The new reference is on line 3, which the parser omits. A normal control patch correctly returned both added line numbers.

**Failure mode:** Bound-remedy item 3 falls back only when an entry is absent. Here `src/a.ts` has an entry, so item 4 scans line 1 and misses the reference on line 3. Candidate-controlled source text has been interpreted as parser metadata. This affects both Git mode and the presentation adapter.

The scope must include `forward-coverage/diff-lines.ts` and its tests, or another verified extraction mechanism. Missing-entry fallback alone is insufficient.

Reusing the shared parser remains the strongest small design: it avoids duplicate diff logic and supports both callers. Correcting and testing its hunk handling would remove this blocker; returning to a line multiset would not.
